name: Monetary Authority of Singapore

scam_info.sample: Notice: MAS will no longer publish on the Investor Alert List the names and online identifiers (such as websites and messaging channels) of entities who impersonate MAS-regulated financial institutions.
scam_info.notes: Canonical of mas.gov.sg/ial. Data rendered client-side by JS widget (bundle.search-ial.1.0.0.js); MAS publishes no feed/download and its backend search endpoint is undocumented (not called). machine_url is the THIRD-PARTY OpenSanctions daily mirror (CC-BY-NC 4.0): index.json 2026-11-25 HTTP 200 -> 902 targets, 1,947 FtM entities, last_change 2026-11-17, updated 2026-11-24 (artifacts/sg_mas_investor_alert/20261124203206-lin/{source.json,targets.simple.csv,entities.ftm.json}). Earlier survey (sources/01_sg_official.md): 924 entities, 786 with websites, 500 phones, 256 emails; listing dates, no expiry. Page chrome 'Last updated on 17 Sep 2026'. Policy change: impersonators of MAS-regulated FIs no longer added (34 legacy 'impersonates a financial institution' notes).

scam_info.sample: Beware of MAS Impersonation Scams. MAS officials will NEVER do these things over a phone call: Ask you to transfer money; Ask you to disclose bank log-in details; ...
scam_info.notes: Narrative. States gov.sg SMS Sender ID rule and ScamShield Helpline 1799. Its 'latest scam alerts and advisories' link points to on-site search (mas.gov.sg/search?q=scams), not a feed.

scam_info.sample: Joint Advisory on Impersonation Scams Involving Chinese Messaging and Payment Platforms ... victims would receive unsolicited calls from local mobile numbers such as “8xxx xxxx” or “+65 xxxx xxxx”
scam_info.notes: item_count = scam/impersonation/fraudulent-website media releases found by URL keyword in sitemap.xml (7,445 URLs, robots Crawl-delay 2, NO lastmod; 1,843 media-release URLs total), 2018-2025. Newest dated: 2025/copy-of-joint-pnr-on-scams-involving-chinese-messaging-and-payment-platforms (Published 04 April 2025); also 2025/pnr-with-spf-on-ntuc-mas-fi-impersonation (14 Mar 2025), 2025/joint-advisory-on-impersonation-scams (28 Feb 2025), 2023/warning-on-scammers-impersonating-as-mas-officers (21 Dec 2023). 2018-2019 'warning on fraudulent website soliciting bitcoin/cryptocurrency investments' releases show the fake site only as a screenshot image (no domain in text). Date only in body 'Published Date:' text; URL has year only. Listing page (HTTP 200) renders items client-side; no RSS advertised.

scam_info.sample: The Shared Responsibility Framework (SRF) for phishing scams was introduced by MAS and Infocomm Media Development Authority of Singapore (IMDA)...
scam_info.notes: Policy hub (SRF). Lists the 17 banks and the Major Payment Institutions/e-wallets the SRF applies to (useful allowlist of genuine FI names, e.g. 'GPAY NETWORK (S) PTE. LTD. GrabPay'). No scam indicators.

scam_info.sample: Warning: Scammers may impersonate MAS-regulated financial institutions to promote investments or solicit funds, often with unsolicited offers of high returns and little or no risk.
scam_info.notes: Financial Institutions Directory = ALLOWLIST of licensed FIs (name, licence, website, address, phone) browsable per sector (/fid/institution?sector=...). MAS states no public API (per earlier survey); HTML only. eservices.mas.gov.sg has no robots.txt/sitemap (returns HTML).

hotlines: 1799 (ScamShield Helpline, cited on MAS scam page)

notes: official_domains: mas.gov.sg (b, serves site; SGDI lists https://www.mas.gov.sg); moneysense.gov.sg (b, linked from MAS page navigation; MAS financial-education programme). mastx.mas.gov.sg (MAS-Tx eServices) seen in nav. Only IOC-bearing official list in partition is the IAL. No RSS/Atom on MAS (none advertised on news page).
